## Parent

#1090

## What to build

Exercise selected Rust/PostgreSQL unsafe boundaries under one supported assertion and sanitizer configuration. Reuse real workloads for tuple conversion with NULL and large values, PostgreSQL errors followed by continued use, cancellation during work, and worker cleanup or restart. Select the actual unsafe adapters reached by those workloads. Check role and search-path restoration independently of sanitizer output.

Initial target: Linux x86_64, PostgreSQL 18 built with `--enable-cassert`, and AddressSanitizer instrumentation for the PostgreSQL process and Rust extension. Use one dedicated Testcontainers image. First prove that the image boots, reports assertions enabled, and catches a controlled invalid-memory fixture; if that combination is not viable, record the concrete failure and select one supported replacement before expanding workloads. This is an instrumented build, separate from the release package.

Initial boundaries on current `main`: `refresh::pipeline::copy_table_rows` for tuple and datum lifetime with NULL and large values; `api::security_context::with_stream_owner_context` and `with_caller_context` for PostgreSQL ERROR unwinding and role/search-path restoration; and `scheduler::dispatch::pg_trickle_refresh_worker_main` for cancellation and worker cleanup. These named workloads bound the first slice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A controlled invalid-memory fixture is detected, and selected extension workloads run without unexplained assertion or sanitizer failures or blanket suppressions.
- [ ] Tests check post-error state and security-context restoration.
- [ ] Changes touching selected unsafe adapters trigger the relevant checks; the full bounded slice runs for release qualification.
- [ ] #1093 records instrumented-build results separately from exact-release runtime tests. Instrumentation is not represented as execution of the unmodified shipped library.

## Blocked by

- #1092 for witnessed failure and cancellation cases.
- #1093 for final release qualification evidence; implementation and local instrumented checks can begin independently.

Apply relevant adapter checks before shipping #1097 or another affected change; safety is not a final cleanup phase.

## Historical context

Replaces the retained scope of #1054 and applicable adapter checks from #1088. All-platform sanitizer support and review of every unsafe block are deferred.

# Acceptance contract: #1098

Contract revision: v1
Source: [#1098](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1098), What to build and acceptance criteria; [#1090](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1090), working agreement and completion
Parent contract: [#1090](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1090) v1
Parent snapshot: #1090 acceptance-contract:1090:v1 block in the canonical issue body; SHA-256: c5645654a11745aee1b64549f457348a145cc9dd10d009b351c2ea89c256d982
Contribution: Refines #1090 v1:Q1090-R01, Q1090-R03, and Q1090-R05 for selected unsafe boundaries and separate instrumented qualification.
Prerequisites: #1092 witnessed failure/cancellation controls are PROVEN in its issue report; #1093 instrumented-build reporting is required for final release qualification, not for implementation or local instrumented checks. Final release evidence must distinguish instrumented results from exact-release runtime tests.

Intended outcome: Exercise selected Rust/PostgreSQL unsafe boundaries under one supported assertion and sanitizer configuration. Reuse real workloads for tuple conversion with NULL and large values, PostgreSQL errors followed by continued use, cancellation during work, and worker cleanup or restart. Select the actual unsafe adapters reached by those workloads. Check role and search-path restoration independently of sanitizer output.

## Evidence context

Anchors: [pipeline copy](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/src/refresh/pipeline.rs),
[security context](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/src/api/security_context.rs),
[worker dispatch](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/src/scheduler/dispatch.rs), and the existing
[E2E Dockerfile](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/tests/Dockerfile.e2e).
Proposed target: `tests/e2e_unsafe_boundary_tests.rs`. Proposed build definition:
`tests/Dockerfile.e2e-asan`. Both are new. The existing security-context
`#[pg_test]` cases do not execute merely because an E2E target is selected.
The live assertion check is `SHOW debug_assertions`, whose result must be `on`.
PostgreSQL documents this as the build's assertion status in
[PG18 preset options](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/runtime-config-preset.html#GUC-DEBUG-ASSERTIONS).

## Implementation decision

Implementation decision: Build tests/Dockerfile.e2e-asan as a dedicated Linux x86_64 image from a pinned PostgreSQL 18.6 source tarball. Configure PostgreSQL with --enable-cassert and AddressSanitizer using -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer, compile the Rust extension with a pinned nightly toolchain and -Zsanitizer=address, and run with ASAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:abort_on_error=1:detect_leaks=1. The first concrete commands are docker build --platform=linux/amd64 -f tests/Dockerfile.e2e-asan -t pg_trickle_e2e_asan:contract . and PGS_E2E_IMAGE=pg_trickle_e2e_asan:contract cargo test --test e2e_unsafe_boundary_tests --features pg18 -- --test-threads=1. The isolated test-only invalid-memory probe must exit nonzero with an ASan diagnostic; the workload run must query SHOW debug_assertions and retain raw logs. If this exact build is infeasible, retain the build failure and choose a supported replacement before widening the workload scope.

## Acceptance matrix

| ID | Source | Requirement | Boundaries / counterexamples | Seam | Oracle | Planned evidence | Plan state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1098-R01 | [#1098](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1098), W | The selected instrumented configuration boots and loads the extension with assertions enabled. | Only PostgreSQL or only Rust is instrumented, assertions are off, or sanitizer runtime cannot load. | Dedicated instrumented PostgreSQL Testcontainer | Live debug_assertions=on and binary instrumentation | `test_instrumented_pg18_boot_and_assertions_enabled`. Dedicated Linux x86_64 Testcontainer, PG18 `--enable-cassert`, ASan on server and extension. Retain both build flag sets/runtime identity, inspect both binaries for actual ASan instrumentation, and query live `debug_assertions`. Add the instrumented PostgreSQL 18 image and launch recipe as the first implementation task. | planned |
| Q1098-R02 | [#1098](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1098), W/AC1 | A controlled invalid-memory operation is detected by the configuration. | Probe never executes or process exits for an unrelated setup error. | Isolated instrumented invalid-memory fixture | Known invalid-memory fault site and ASan diagnostic | `test_instrumented_invalid_memory_probe_is_detected`. Require the expected ASan error class, fault-site diagnostic, and unsuccessful probe execution in an isolated test-only fixture. Identify the probed binary; use direct binary instrumentation evidence for both server and extension from R01, or a scoped probe in each. Keep probes outside shipped artifacts. Run this case after the instrumented image exists. | planned |
| Q1098-R03 | [#1098](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1098), W/AC1 | The actual tuple-copy adapter preserves NULL and large-value rows through repeated work. | Workload takes a fallback path or lifetime error corrupts a later row. | Instrumented refresh/tuple-copy SQL | Independent public bag/schema query and clean diagnostics | `test_pipeline_copy_null_and_toasted_rows_survive_refresh`. Reach `copy_table_rows` with mixed NULLs and toasted text, then insert/update/delete and repeat refresh. Require exact public bag/schema equality and no unexplained assertion/ASan diagnostic. Add an adapter-path witness, then run this case in the instrumented image. | planned |
| Q1098-R04 | [#1098](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1098), W/AC2 | PostgreSQL ERROR inside owner context restores authorization state. | Role, `search_path`, or `row_security` leaks after the error. | Instrumented owner-context SQL on one backend | Pre-error same-backend role, search_path and row_security | `test_owner_context_pg_error_restores_state_and_continues`. Reach `with_stream_owner_context`, witness the expected ERROR, compare same-backend `current_user`, `current_setting('role')`, `search_path`, and `row_security` with baseline, then perform an allowed and a denied operation under the restored permissions. Run this case in the instrumented image after adding an adapter-path witness. | planned |
| Q1098-R05 | [#1098](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1098), W/AC2 | PostgreSQL ERROR inside caller context restores authorization state. | Only `row_security` is checked while role/search path remain altered. | Instrumented caller-context SQL on one backend | Pre-error same-backend role, search_path and row_security | `test_caller_context_pg_error_restores_state_and_continues`. Repeat the preceding same-backend checks through `with_caller_context`, including successful continued use and the expected denied operation. Explicitly arrange adapter execution; existing private pg_tests alone are insufficient. Run this case in the instrumented image after adding an adapter-path witness. | planned |
| Q1098-R06 | [#1098](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1098), W/AC1/AC2 | Cancellation of an active dispatched worker leaves recoverable state and permits later work. | Cancel hits an idle/completed backend; worker slot/permit stays occupied or committed output corrupts. | Instrumented dispatched worker and refresh SQL | Committed checkpoint and available worker capacity after cancellation | `test_dispatch_worker_cancel_cleanup_and_restart_recovers`. Witness `pg_trickle_refresh_worker_main` doing the selected job, cancel and observe its error, inspect job/slot reconciliation, then require replacement work to finish and exact public results to recover. Reuse #1092 witness controls. Run this case in the instrumented image after adding an adapter-path witness. | planned |
| Q1098-R07 | [#1098](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1098), AC1 | Passing instrumented evidence contains no unexplained failures or blanket suppression. | ASan emits errors but the runner exits 0, or all adapter reports are suppressed. | Instrumented run logs and exit status | Raw ASan/assertion diagnostics; probe isolated from workloads | `check_instrumented_diagnostics`. Scan retained raw logs and exit outcomes for the selected workloads. Reject unexplained reports, missing logs, or blanket suppression configuration. Keep expected probe diagnostics identified separately from production-workload results. | planned |
| Q1098-R08 | [#1098](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1098), AC3 | Changes to the selected adapters trigger the relevant instrumented checks. | A source change to pipeline, security context, or dispatch bypasses the job. | PR CI changed-path routing | Selected source paths and required instrumented case mapping | `check_unsafe_boundary_ci_routing` at the existing CI contract entry point. For each named source path, a changed-file fixture must select its instrumented cases; a disabled/removed route fails. Run affected checks before shipping LSN adapters that touch these boundaries. | planned |
| Q1098-R09 | [#1098](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1098), W/AC3 | Release qualification executes the full bounded instrumented slice or explicitly remains incomplete. | Boot/probe passes but one workload is missing, or an unsupported configuration is silently replaced by ordinary smoke tests. | Release qualification evidence | R01-R06 case inventory and separate instrumented build identity | `check_unsafe_release_slice_complete` in #1093. Require R01-R06 case identities plus diagnostic validation. If initial instrumentation is infeasible, retain the concrete failure and select a supported replacement with the same detection/workload obligations before claiming acceptance. Results remain separate under Q1093-R11. | planned |

## Unresolved gaps

- None. The image, probe, launch command, and failure oracle are now explicit contract inputs; implementation must still build and run them.

## Open questions

- None. The contract starts with Linux x86_64 PostgreSQL 18.6 cassert plus ASan and requires an explicit replacement decision only if that build fails.

## Out of scope

- All-platform sanitizer support and review of every unsafe block.

## Change notes

- The v1 planning inputs are now explicit: a pinned PostgreSQL 18.6 source build, Rust sanitizer build, isolated probe, and exact launch commands. Requirement meanings are unchanged.- Initial contract, v1. Existing matrix IDs Q1098-R01–Q1098-R09 retain their meanings; GitHub issue history preserves the prior matrix. The original acceptance checkboxes remain source criteria, not proof.

## Storage handoff

Canonical destination: this issue body, revision v1. Reread this saved issue before use.

## Implementation handoff

Implement the smallest complete solution inside the spec envelope. Preserve requirement IDs and promised outcomes.

## Proof handoff

Evaluate every requirement against this contract revision and one fixed candidate. Record actual evidence and verdicts in a separate proof report.
